name.text: Sketch the graph of a quadratic (drag the parabola)

questiontext.text:
Sketch the graph of \[ y = {@qexpr@}. \]

Drag the red point \(V\) to the vertex (turning point), and drag the red point \(W\) to any other point the curve passes through.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ansV="rV" input-ref-ansW="rW" width="540px" height="540px"]] var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-6.5, 12.5, 6.5, -12.5], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); var V = brd.create('point',[-4,4],{name:'V',color:'#cc0000',fillColor:'#cc0000',size:5,snapToGrid:true,snapSizeX:1,snapSizeY:1,label:{offset:[8,8],cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}}); var W = brd.create('point',[-3,5],{name:'W',color:'#cc0000',fillColor:'#cc0000',size:5,snapToGrid:true,snapSizeX:1,snapSizeY:1,label:{offset:[8,8],cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}}); function af(){ var dx=W.X()-V.X(); if (Math.abs(dx)<1e-6) return null; return (W.Y()-V.Y())/(dx*dx); } brd.create('functiongraph',[function(x){ var a=af(); if (a===null) return NaN; return a*(x-V.X())*(x-V.X()) + V.Y(); }, -6.5, 6.5],{strokeColor:'#1f4fd8', strokeWidth:2.5, highlight:false}); stack_jxg.bind_point(rV, V); stack_jxg.bind_point(rW, W); [[/jsxgraph]]
[[input:ansV]] [[validation:ansV]] [[input:ansW]] [[validation:ansW]]
[[feedback:prtVertex]] [[feedback:prtShape]]

generalfeedback.text:
How to sketch \(y={@qexpr@}\):

  1. Direction.

    The coefficient of \(x^2\) is \(a={@a@}\), so the parabola opens [[ if test="is(a>0)" ]] upwards [[ else ]] downwards [[/ if ]].

  2. Vertex.

    Completing the square gives \(y={@a@}(x-({@h@}))^2 + ({@k@})\)

    Therefore, the vertex is at \(({@h@},\,{@k@})\).

  3. x-intercepts (roots).

    Solving \(y=0\) gives \(x={@r1@}\) and \(x={@r2@}\).

  4. y-intercept.

    Putting \(x=0\) gives \(y={@cc@}\), i.e. the point \((0,\,{@cc@})\).

  5. Sketch.

    Plot the vertex, the two roots and the y-intercept, then draw a smooth parabola through them.

[[jsxgraph width="500px" height="500px"]] var A={#a#}, H={#h#}, K={#k#}, R1={#r1#}, R2={#r2#}, CC={#cc#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-6.5, 12.5, 6.5, -12.5], axis:true, grid:true, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false, keepaspectratio:false}); brd.create('functiongraph',[function(x){ return A*(x-H)*(x-H) + K; }, -6.5, 6.5],{strokeColor:'#1f4fd8', strokeWidth:2.5, highlight:false}); brd.create('point',[H,K],{name:'vertex',fixed:true,color:'#cc0000',fillColor:'#cc0000',size:4,label:{offset:[8,-4],cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}}); brd.create('point',[R1,0],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#2ca02c',fillColor:'#2ca02c',size:3}); brd.create('point',[R2,0],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#2ca02c',fillColor:'#2ca02c',size:3}); brd.create('point',[0,CC],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#000000',fillColor:'#000000',size:3}); [[/jsxgraph]]

feedbackvariables.text: dxp : ansW[1] - ansV[1]; as : if is(dxp=0) then 999 else (ansW[2]-ansV[2])/dxp^2;

falsefeedback.text: Check the coefficient \(a={@a@}\): it fixes how steep the parabola is and whether it opens up or down. Place \(W\) on the curve, e.g. one step right of the vertex at \(({@Wtx@},{@Wty@})\).

feedbackvariables.text: hs : round(ansV[1]); ks : round(ansV[2]); vok : if (is(hs=h) and is(ks=k)) then 1 else 0;

falsefeedback.text: The vertex is at the turning point. Complete the square (or use \(x=-\frac{b}{2a}\)) to find it: the vertex should be \(({@h@},{@k@})\).
